newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria domestic debt rises 59.44 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria domestic debt rises 59.44 pct in January.

text.p: Bulgaria's domestic debt surged by some 626 billion levs in January to 1.679 trillion levs because of the fall in the lev and new government securities issued to bridge a budget gap, ministry figures showed.

"The debt rose some 60 percent last month mainly because of the lev fall, which boosted the price of dollar-denominated bad debt bonds and deposit guarantee bonds," a finance ministry official told Reuters.
Some 550 billion levs of the January rise were due to the lev depreciation, figures showed. @

The lev fell to 1,022 per dollar on January 31 from 487 a month earlier in the central bank daily dollar fixing used in the calculations. It traded near 2,800 per dollar on the local interbank market on Monday.
Net sales of government securities in January totalled some 64.5 billion levs.
The finance ministry also received 12 billion levs of short-term loans from the central bank last month and 1.2 billion levs from the State Savings Bank, figures showed. @

The finance ministry has issued $79 million of floater coupon T-bonds last year to guarantee foreign currency deposits of companies and individuals in five of the 13 local banks, against which the central bank has filed insolvency suits.
Bad debt bonds worth 32 billion levs and $1.8 billion respectively were issued two years ago to cover banks' non-performing loans extended to state companies before 1991.
The total par value of dollar-denominated bad debt bonds in circulation at end-January was $950 million and lev-denominated bonds amounted to around 20 billion levs. @
